title: 2021 AMC 12A Problem 7
statement: What is the least possible value of \((xy - 1)^2 + (x + y)^2\) for real numbers \(x\) and \(y?\)

solutions.text:
Expanding, \[ \begin{aligned} &(xy-1)^2 + (x+y)^2 \\ &= x^2y^2 - 2xy + 1 + x^2 \\ &\quad {}+ 2xy + y^2 \\ &= x^2y^2 + x^2 + y^2 + 1. \end{aligned} \] This factors as \((x^2 + 1)(y^2 + 1).\)

Each factor is at least \(1,\) so the product is at least \(1,\) with equality when \(x = y = 0.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Expand fully; the cross terms \(-2xy\) and \(+2xy\) cancel
The expression equals \((x^2 + 1)(y^2 + 1),\) a product of two factors each at least \(1\)
